title: Socio-Culturally Aware Evaluation Framework for LLM-Based Content Moderation

bias_targets.methodology: Conditioning LLMs on different religious personas (e.g., Protestant, Taoist, Baptist, Atheist) and categorizing the generated statements to measure the proportion of hateful versus supportive content.

Prompting LLMs with specific political ideologies and social beliefs (e.g., Right-leaning, Socialist, Libertarian) to analyze variations in the hatefulness of statements and the persuasiveness of generated misinformation.
Evaluating the tendency of LLMs to either spread or debunk misinformation when conditioned on different professional roles (e.g., thought leaders, activists, journalists, scientists).
Measuring the influence of a persona's immigrant status on content generation by evaluating how accurately an LLM can predict the immigrant attribute solely from the generated text.
Assessing the impact of a persona's age group on generated content by predicting the age attribute directly from the stylistic and linguistic features of the LLM's outputs.

Generating targeted hate speech datasets spanning over 300 socio-cultural targets (including various racial and ethnic groups) and evaluating the zero-shot moderation classification accuracy of different LLMs on these diverse targets.

Testing LLM content moderation systems using synthetically generated text that includes implicit and explicit hate speech or sexual content directed at various gender identities and sexual orientations.
